head_note: HEAD advanced concurrently during this read-only task. Listed production source hashes remain the same as the original inspected source. No checkout or production edit was made.
verification: Static source review and official API documentation only. No game, GPU, build, native launch, or new runtime verification. Proposed tests were not run by this agent.
conclusion: Use immutable per-dispatch CB/descriptor storage owned by a command-list recording epoch. Retire an epoch only after successful Reset or object destruction detaches the recording AND every possible observed submission has completed. Existing RRTrace callbacks/state cannot be reused unchanged to claim unconditional safety for arbitrary valid delayed submission: hook coverage, proxy identity, object destruction, resubmission, and queue completion must first be addressed. Unknown coverage/failure must retain accepted resources and refuse new work at a finite budget.

current_storage_and_callback_evidence.finding: ComputeState has persistently mapped upload slots and per-slot shader-visible heaps. Dispatch memcpy and descriptor creation overwrite the selected slot before modulo advance; commands reference GPU addresses/handles rather than immutable CB/heap snapshots. Destructor unmaps/releases its owned storage without a submission fence.
CreateSRVs/CreateUAVs write descriptor contents at the selected CPU heap handles.

FrameDescriptorHeap owns raw heap pointers and releases them in its destructor. A new packet should be move-only and use explicit ComPtr ownership; copying this raw-owning helper is not a sound lease implementation.

Capture path demonstrates retaining scratch/input/output resources, upload, all descriptor heaps, root signature and PSO in a ticket. Its dedicated 12-slot shader and capture ownership are not a generic production lifetime solution.

Useful Retain and Before/After submission pattern. Registry intentionally survives static teardown, allows only four unresolved captures, and strongly owns command-list identity. This self-pin prevents final command-list destruction from being observable. Reset notifications currently update tickets only.

Current state marks repeated submission ambiguous and unreleasable. It tracks one fence expected value, not independent unordered queue completions. Do not remove the repeated-submit quarantine and then treat one max fence value as proof that multiple queues are complete.

Both inspected ExecuteCommandLists branches call BeforeSubmission, original Execute, AfterSubmission. Reset calls original first and notifies only on success. No bypass inside these branches was found; coverage of all actual method implementations remains unproven.

Hooks are installed using temporary DIRECT objects and single global method addresses. EnsureRRTraceHooks only tests non-null original pointers. Failed command-list detour commit clears several pointers but leaves o_Reset set, admitting a false positive. Real-object unwrap returns a borrowed pointer after releasing its query ref. Optional hook teardown can detach Reset. Proxy/canonical identity and actual COMPUTE/custom implementation coverage must be proven or resources quarantined.
Opaque native denoiser context is destroyed directly by the feature; retaining visible CB/heap objects alone cannot keep opaque native resources alive after arbitrary feature release.
Evaluate returns recording result without waiting on a title queue. Feature release erases its owning context without completion retirement.
DelayedDestroy is a detached two-second sleep, not evidence of GPU completion.

recommended_minimal_package.scope: Correct lifetime and immutable inputs for OptiScaler-owned preprocessor CB/descriptor storage. Do not promise arbitrary out-of-order native RR/shared scratch semantics. Existing caller must still provide valid resource states and ordered/synchronized executions of a shared native context.
recommended_minimal_package.compute_state: Replace fixed-slot overwrite with per-dispatch immutable upload/descriptor slices. Allocate/retain the slice, referenced resources, root signature and PSO in the recording epoch before the first referencing command. A pooled arena can be reused only after the epoch retirement predicate, never by frame modulo. GPU addresses and descriptor handles remain stable for the entire executable epoch.
recommended_minimal_package.preflight: Reserve the maximum permitted evaluation packet before any FSRD conversion command so allocation/budget failure does not leave a partially recorded helper chain. Ordinary enabled path has seed1 + filter5 + conversion1 + compose1 = 8 dispatches, 2304 aligned CB bytes and 73 descriptors; debug compose+blit upper bound is 9 dispatches, 2560 CB bytes and 87 descriptors. Confirm this bound when changing branch structure. Trace-owned additive shader storage remains separately owned.
recommended_minimal_package.identity_and_object_death: Attach a private IUnknown epoch manager to the canonical real ID3D12GraphicsCommandList using SetPrivateDataInterface with a dedicated GUID. Manager owns the current recording epoch. Registry owns epochs/packets but must not strongly retain the command list, avoiding a reference cycle. Attachment destruction marks detachment on object death/overwrite. GetPrivateData temporary references must be balanced; their release must not be mistaken for object death. Use a retained, uniform canonical real-object query at arm, submission and Reset; do not use only proxy IUnknown identity or the existing borrowed unwrap result.
recommended_minimal_package.reset: On successful original Reset, detach the exact old epoch, then make a new epoch lazily for the new recording. Failed Reset changes nothing. Old submitted epoch remains alive across re-recording until its completion requirements finish. Reset can legally occur before old GPU execution completes; allocator reset has a different restriction.
recommended_minimal_package.submission: Before original Execute, obtain strong references to the exact current recording epochs and register pending submission requirements under the registry lock. After original Execute, signal a fresh fence value 1 on that actual queue for that submission, then bind the result to those same old epoch references. Do not look up the mutable current epoch after Execute. One fresh fence per Execute can be shared by all matched epochs. Never hold registry locks across queue COM calls. Exceptions/allocation failure before original Execute still require conservative unknown-submission quarantine because the caller's Execute must continue.
recommended_minimal_package.resubmission_and_threads: A closed recording may be validly resubmitted after prior execution completes, so first completion alone cannot release its packet while the recording is still attached. Add one completion requirement per observed submission; do not permanently quarantine normal valid repeat submission. Different queues need independent fences; a higher completed value on a fast queue does not establish another queue's completion. Concurrent hooks serialize metadata updates, preserve old epoch references, and permit independent queue work. Validity/ordering of native shared state remains the caller's responsibility.
recommended_minimal_package.retirement_predicate: Detached recording AND zero pending Signal bindings AND no unknown submission/fence failure AND every registered fence has a finite completed value at least its signaled value. With proven complete Execute coverage, never-submitted detached epochs may retire immediately; without that proof they remain quarantined. Preserve accepted resources on every uncertain path.
recommended_minimal_package.hook_requirements: Use committed hook-install flags/target-address coverage rather than non-null trampolines. Track the actual canonical command-list Reset implementation and all actual non-copy queue Execute implementations that can receive accepted recordings, including COMPUTE/proxy forwarding. The current temporary-DIRECT/global-address installation does not prove this. Separate required lifetime hooks from optional HUD/trace teardown; do not uninstall while executable epochs or pending completion requirements exist. If future queue coverage cannot be guaranteed, bounded permanent retention is the only safe fallback for accepted recordings; do not infer discard from an absent Execute callback.
recommended_minimal_package.budget_and_failure: Finite budget cannot accept an unbounded amount of arbitrarily deferred work. Account unreleased storage; refuse a new evaluation before helper commands if immutable allocation/coverage/budget checks fail. Do not enlarge the modulo ring, wait on an unseen queue, or free old leases to make room. Fence creation/Signal failure, missing callbacks, canonicalization failure, or unexpected hook teardown pins affected epochs and prevents unsafe reuse; report/refuse subsequent work. UINT64_MAX is device removal, not successful completion. Terminal device teardown may release only under an explicit permanently-unusable-device owner contract, not a normal frame-completion heuristic or static/DLL shutdown.
recommended_minimal_package.feature_destruction: To support arbitrary deferred feature/context destruction as well as CB/heap lifetime, move native/preprocessor GPU owners into a retirement bundle retained by their recorded epochs, or require a documented caller drain before feature release. No raw Feature/ComputeState pointer callbacks. CPU history notifications use weak/shared state. The current immediate native DestroyContext and two-second delayed destroy cannot satisfy the broader guarantee.
recommended_minimal_package.why_not_plain_existing_ticket: Its retained resources are useful, but four-capture cap, strong list identity, repeated-submit quarantine, single expected fence model and export-oriented Ready/Invalid rules are unsuitable unchanged. Implement a small generic recording-lifetime state and keep trace export validity independent. Current callbacks alone are insufficient for an unconditional production guarantee.

root_constants.conclusion: SetComputeRoot32BitConstants could snapshot entire seed/filter/compose CB payloads after corresponding root signatures change; conversion cannot fit the 64-DWORD limit. Root constants do not snapshot shader-visible descriptor contents. Thus this is a partial alternative, not a minimal complete remedy.

history_and_drop_policy.current_evidence: Native CPU camera/view/jitter and valid bit commit at FSRDFeature_Dx12.cpp:1922 and 4078–4086 after native API records commands. Composition read index flips only on successful Evaluate closure at 2071 via guard 1733–1738 and FinishCompositionHistory 1986–1994. Neither commit proves submission.
history_and_drop_policy.dropped_epoch: If complete Execute coverage proves an epoch detached with zero prior submission intents, it was discarded. Schedule invalidation of native and composition CPU history for the next relevant Evaluate; never mutate already-recorded immutable CBs. If an old epoch has already registered submission/pending Signal, successful Reset is normal re-recording and must not by itself invalidate its submitted history.
history_and_drop_policy.basis_tracking: Associate history with a recording epoch and serial/reset basis. Notify only when a discarded epoch is still the basis of future CPU state; an old unrelated discarded epoch must not invalidate a newer independently reset basis. If a predecessor recording is a different epoch and has not yet submitted, conservatively reset native/motion/compose history while recording its successor. Already-recorded dependent jobs cannot be repaired by a later CPU invalidation callback. Same-epoch command order/all-or-none discard allows ordinary continuation. Submitted predecessors still require caller queue ordering/synchronization.
history_and_drop_policy.available_helper: FSRDFeatureDx12::InvalidateDenoiserHistory() is private noexcept at FSRDFeature_Dx12.h:336–340; it calls public FSRDPreprocessor_Dx12::InvalidateCompositionHistory() (.h:332; .cpp:1981–1983), sets _hasDenoiserHistory=false and _lastDispatchRequestedReset=false. Next conversion selects current jitter as previous and disables motion history at 3267–3273; native setup zeroes camera delta at 2097–2100 and sets FFX_DENOISER_DISPATCH_RESET at 2176–2177.
history_and_drop_policy.limit: These changes do not repair resource content races or native internal state after arbitrary out-of-order execution, nor invalidate FSR31 upscaler history. Lifetime correctness and temporal semantic ordering are separate contracts.

upscale_failure_followup.qualification: Do not claim composition flips on an upscale-false exit. Its existing guard success remains false until line 2071, so 2068–2069 already calls FinishCompositionHistory(false) on scope exit. Original H2 remains distinct: successful Evaluate can commit both CPU histories and later be discarded without submission.
upscale_failure_followup.predicate: DispatchUpscaler returns false at FSR31Feature_Dx12.cpp:697–707 for any non-OK API result. FSRDFeature_Dx12.cpp:2068–2069 returns false after native CommitDenoiserHistory at 1922; it currently leaves _hasDenoiserHistory true. Only FFX_API_RETURN_ERROR_RUNTIME_ERROR requests backend recreation (FSR31Feature_Dx12.cpp:701–704).
upscale_failure_followup.outer_flow: IFeature_Dx12.cpp:244–249 returns false directly. NVNGX_DLSS_Dx12.cpp:1109–1121 logs failure, restores root state and returns NVSDK_NGX_Result_Fail, with no reset/invalidation. Local SDK header nvsdk_ngx.h:414–418 requires an open recording command list and non-copy queue but specifies no failure rollback or mandatory discard.
upscale_failure_followup.small_candidate: Inside the existing !isUpscalerReady branch, call private InvalidateDenoiserHistory() before returning false. The helper already covers both native CPU and composition flags; composition invalidation is redundant with existing guard. No implementation was made here.
upscale_failure_followup.safe_scope: It only changes CPU history flags and does not mutate recorded commands, clear GPU textures, destroy resources, or retroactively affect submitted jobs. Under the existing serialized ordered-evaluation/resource contract it safely requests a conservative RR reset on the next evaluation even if the failed frame's RR work later executes.
upscale_failure_followup.classification: Closes ambiguous retention after reported failure if caller discards the recording; not proof of an unconditional stale native-history defect caused by upscale failure itself. If caller submits the valid RR+composition prefix, the preserved native history could be correct and the reset merely loses temporal accumulation. Does not cure successful-evaluation drop, already-recorded successors, ring overwrite, invalid submission ordering or upscaler internal recovery. Quality acceptance and exact failure injection still required.
upscale_failure_followup.minimal_validation: Inject a non-runtime upscale return failure after successful native record; verify returned Fail, no composition read-index flip, native/helper CPU valid false, next conversion current/previous jitter equal and MotionHistoryValid false, next native RESET set, and normal success still commits. Run two ordered modes: submit failed prefix and discard/reset it before next evaluation. Compare no-error control; do not describe these proposed checks as already run.

cpu_state_tests_proposed: Record at least 4 conversion packets and 10 composition packets before first Execute; all captured CB bytes, GPU addresses and descriptor identities remain immutable and distinct where simultaneously executable.
BeforeSubmission(old), successful Reset, register/record new epoch, AfterSubmission(old): old completion attaches only to old epoch and neither retires early.
Failed Reset leaves current epoch attached; first completed Execute without Reset cannot retire a still-resubmittable closed recording.
Valid sequential resubmission adds a completion requirement; detach waits for all of them without permanent ambiguous-submission leak.
Two independent queues: completion on fast queue never retires work pending on slow queue.
CreateFence/Signal failure, allocation failure in Execute hook, missing coverage, canonical identity failure and device removal quarantine accepted resources; new work is refused within budget.
Final command-list release without Reset detaches via private attachment, retains submitted packets until completion and does not self-pin command-list lifetime.
Proxy and real interfaces resolve one epoch; failed detour commit cannot report installed coverage; required callbacks survive optional hook teardown.
Discard unsubmitted relevant history basis requests reset; submitted Reset and old unrelated discard do not falsely invalidate a newer basis.
smallest_meaningful_lifetime_validation.native_fixture_proposed: Parent's isolated fixture: record more than ring depth production-equivalent dispatches before first GPU Execute/Signal. Use alternating identifiable CBs and input resources; compare CB/input fingerprints and output against dedicated immutable per-dispatch CB/descriptor arm. Require immutable arm to match sequential baseline while cyclic arm demonstrably aliases when vulnerable. Add Reset/re-record with a fresh allocator while old GPU work is pending and verify no premature lease destruction. No game evidence is inferred.
smallest_meaningful_lifetime_validation.pass_criteria: All accepted dispatches preserve captured constants/descriptors until their recording cannot execute again and all actual submissions complete. No unsafe release on missing/failed fence, no false discard on Before/After Reset race, no history reset merely because an already-submitted recording is reset, and bounded rejection occurs before new helper commands. Source-only proof is not a substitute for these checks.

official_api_sources.claim: 64-DWORD root signature maximum; tables cost one, root constants one per DWORD, root descriptors two; root versioning does not version descriptor heap/buffer contents.
Command-list Reset may occur while its previous execution is still on GPU; allocator reset differs.
Separate successive Execute calls on a queue order whole executions; valid rereuse requires prior command-list execution no longer be pending. Batch lists may be merged.
Parallel queues require explicit ordering; fence completion determines safe storage reuse.
Private interface attachment is AddRefed and released on object destruction or GUID overwrite.
Reading an attached IUnknown adds a reference that must be released.
UINT64_MAX means device removal, not ordinary completion.
